sourceAssertions: ILlmInvocationPort and its completed-response implementation remain available and compatible; streaming is additive.
Provider wire framing stays in concrete provider drivers and no Web/SSE/provider-wire type crosses ILlmStreamingInvocationPort.
OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, and Ollama implement IProviderStreamingChatCompletionDriver through the existing ChatCompletion capability.
The adapter selects incremental delivery only when the profile and driver permit it; otherwise a completed driver uses CompletedFallback.
RetryScheduled is false after any accepted delta, and the provider dispatch is not reissued.
Each actual dispatch emits one started ordinal and one deterministic terminal outcome consumed by durable audit.
No new production partial class, forbidden reference, or dependency cycle exists.

acceptance.criterion: Existing ILlmInvocationPort callers remain source- and behavior-compatible.
acceptance.evidence: The unchanged completed adapter suite is included in the final 86/86 union; ILlmStreamingInvocationPort is a separate additive registration.

acceptance.criterion: OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, and Ollama produce incremental text through one provider-neutral contract.
acceptance.evidence: Fragmented protocol tests prove OpenAI Chat Completions/Responses, Azure OpenAI, and Ollama yield ProviderChatTextDelta plus ProviderChatCompleted through one adapter contract.

acceptance.criterion: A non-incremental supported driver uses a deterministic single-delta fallback or typed unsupported result.
acceptance.evidence: The completed-only driver test yields exactly AttemptStarted, one delta, and Completed, both labelled CompletedFallback.

acceptance.criterion: No automatic retry occurs after the first emitted delta.
acceptance.evidence: StreamAsync_never_retries_after_a_delta_is_visible proves one call followed by a terminal failed update; retry is guarded by !emittedDelta.

acceptance.criterion: Every actual provider dispatch attempt receives a distinct monotonic audit ordinal and deterministic outcome.
acceptance.evidence: The retry test proves ordinals 1 and 2; Streaming_audit_records_each_actual_attempt_with_its_own_usage_and_ordinal proves two distinct durable rows and attempt-local usage.

acceptance.criterion: Streaming failures expose no credentials, raw frames, or raw provider errors.
acceptance.evidence: Malformed-frame, raw-provider-secret, and hidden-reasoning tests prove public updates/messages contain no raw frames, provider detail, credential, or reasoning text.

bugs: A bounded channel bridge was required so the task-based provider runtime retains its dispatch lane throughout asynchronous enumeration.
Attempt-local usage was separated from aggregate retry usage before durable audit.
Runtime preparation failures are now sanitized without creating a false provider-attempt row.
SupportsStreaming=false now forces deterministic completed fallback.
deviations: Five focused test commands exceeded the normal four-command budget. One command failed at compile because the new direct logging-abstractions reference required restore; after the first final union, review found runtime-preparation sanitization and profile fallback defects, so one additional identical focused union was run at the final implementation head. No broad test lane ran.
The first sandboxed project restore could not read the user NuGet configuration; the unchanged authorized restore succeeded. No package version changed.
Three affected build commands were used and all passed with zero warnings/errors.
knownGaps: SB08 must connect the proven streaming/audit updates to a bounded durable event journal and operation finalization.
SSE transport, disconnect behavior, and Last-Event-ID replay remain locked to SB09.
Cross-platform focused proof remains owned by SB11.
